subject: distribution-core-leftover-join.v1

verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 0 advisories.
acceptanceGrade: ACCEPT-CLEAN. The obligation set is a complete verbatim decomposition of DR-101's own two register cells, the split is correct against v16, and every not-that-gate distinction holds against live claims.

coverageAudit.method: Set-compared the join's obligation ids against v16's registerRowQuoted.obligationDecomposition, then checked that decomposition against DR-101's live register cells.
coverageAudit.summaryPartition: Two leftover (OBL-D1, OBL-D2) plus five capable-of-riding; the union equals the obligation set exactly and the intersection is empty. No obligation is dropped and none is double-counted.
coverageAudit.decompositionIsItselfComplete: v16's fragments are verbatim from DR-101's live row. The evidence cell reads 'Reviewed closure inventory and dependency graph; gate harnesses DR-G01–G05', which is exactly OBL-1 and OBL-2. The claim cell reads 'Native signed distribution-core language, mandatory closure/TCB inventory, layering, signing/notarization, platforms', which is exactly OBL-D1, OBL-D-INV, OBL-D-LAY, OBL-D2 and OBL-D3. So the seven obligations exhaust both cells with nothing left unclassified.

splitAudit.leftoverIsCorrect: v16 marks OBL-D1 'RESERVED, not decided' and OBL-D2 'Signing ROLE list extracted; ceremony/notarization RESERVED', and its namedOpenDecisions carry OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 with owner 'a later successor, not this extraction'. The join's aliasing of OBL-D1 to OD-101-1 and OBL-D2 to OD-101-2 matches v16's own answeredAt pointers.
splitAudit.ridingIsCorrect: Each riding obligation's reason names the v16 field that answers it, and each matches: OBL-1 at threeCores / defaultInstall / inventorySchema, OBL-2 at gatesG01G05, OBL-D-INV at inventorySchema.everyReleaseMustPublish, OBL-D-LAY at inventorySchema.layerTaxonomy — the join also cites graphRules, which is a real sibling field in that schema — and OBL-D3 at platforms.
splitAudit.platformsClaim: v16's platforms are macos/arm64, macos/x86_64, linux/x86_64 and linux/arm64 with Windows deliberately absent and warrant D-002, so the join's 'D-002 four-platform set' and 'does not change D-002 platforms' are both accurate.
splitAudit.g22Claim: v16's ID-DEP-K2 is the qualitative OS ABI/loader/libc/cert/font/ICU allowlist riding on DR-126 / G22, which is exactly what the OBL-D-INV reason says, and G22's live claim is 'Executed closure uses only declared platform TCB dependencies'.

gateOwnershipAudit.g01g05DoNotOwnLanguage: Live claims are: G01 distribution core is small; G02 minimal mandatory closure/TCB is bounded; G03 --help/--version remain fast; G04 baseline/peak RSS is bounded; G05 each component cost is independently visible. None mentions language, Rust, notarization or signing ceremony. The join's assertion that they measure size, startup, memory and component delta but own no language choice is verified against the cells, not inferred.
gateOwnershipAudit.g13IsNotCoreLanguage: G13's live claim is 'Each supported language/tooling role delivers language-native quality rather than a lowest-common-denominator abstraction', which is per-role quality and not core-language selection, as the join says.
gateOwnershipAudit.g30DoesNotOwnCoreInventory: G30's live claim itself carries 'Not DR-101 signed-distribution-core inventory', so the join's file08Pin note is corroborated by the register rather than merely asserted.
gateOwnershipAudit.g01g05AreNamed: All five harness cells begin 'named:' and all five carry owner cells, so the join's 'already named (D-086/D-088/D-102)' holds on current standing — including G03 and G04, whose identifiers were once reserved and were later named under D-102.

selfCorrectionsDuringReview.nearMiss: I was close to charging a SHOULD-FIX against executionObligationOwnerToday.
selfCorrectionsDuringReview.reasoning: The field reads 'Architecture + release engineering' on every riding obligation, while the live gate owner cells are heterogeneous — G01, G03 and G04 are Release engineering, G02 is Architecture + release, and G05 is Component publisher + release. Read as a summary of the five gates' owners it would be over-inclusive for four and would drop Component publisher at G05, which matters because D-056 gate 3 turns on the remainder being named at an obligation with an owner.
selfCorrectionsDuringReview.whyItWasWrong: I checked DR-101's row before writing the finding. Its owner cell is exactly 'Architecture + release engineering', byte-for-byte. The field is the row's execution-obligation owner, not a roll-up of gate owners, and it is correct.
selfCorrectionsDuringReview.lesson: Recorded because the finding would have been confidently argued and wrong, and because the check that killed it took one read. After missing two real defects earlier in this session there is pressure to charge; the answer to that pressure is more verification, not a lower bar.

consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: It binds NOTHING and changes no status, and DR-101's live status is OPEN. Status recitals belong to the recording entry, which is where the sibling DR-117 and DR-131 chains put them.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The OBL-D-LAY reason cites graphRules where v16's answeredAt names only inventorySchema.layerTaxonomy
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: graphRules is a real sibling field of the same schema and does specify layering, so the citation is accurate rather than invented. Charging an artifact for naming more of the relevant law than its pointer strictly required would be perverse.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Extending the review to whether OD-101-1 or OD-101-2 should be decided
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The dispatch forbids deciding either, and the artifact expressly declines to. Both remain a later successor's work under v16's own terms.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Thirteen attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 7b2f2b8c at 0444 unmoved, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean. The subject pins head 0fcf3d3 while live HEAD is 19b5231, and I did not take the PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT instruction on trust — COORD's pre-D-159 bytes are a byte-prefix of the current file, growth is 2163 bytes, and D-159 is the only added heading, with file 08 unmoved. The completeness result is the strong one. The join's seven obligations are exactly v16's decomposition, and that decomposition is a verbatim exhaustion of DR-101's own two register cells: the evidence cell 'Reviewed closure inventory and dependency graph; gate harnesses DR-G01–G05' is OBL-1 and OBL-2, and the claim cell 'Native signed distribution-core language, mandatory closure/TCB inventory, layering, signing/notarization, platforms' is the five decision fragments. The summary partitions all seven with no overlap and no omission. The split is right: v16 marks OBL-D1 RESERVED and OBL-D2 ceremony-and-notarization RESERVED, and its namedOpenDecisions carry OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 — which appear nowhere in file 08 or COORD, so they looked like invention until I found them as v16's own ids under D-114. Every not-that-gate distinction verifies against live claims: G01 through G05 measure size, bounded closure, startup, RSS and per-component cost and mention no language or ceremony; G13 is per-role language quality, not core-language selection; and G30's own claim already carries 'Not DR-101 signed-distribution-core inventory'. Required-now stays 26 and every prohibition token is a refusal. The artifact also states its own D-056 effect — not eligible, gates 2 and 3 not holding — which is the omission Codex caught in the DR-117 naming v2 and is correct here, since the two leftover obligations carry no gate and no owner. One self-correction is recorded because it nearly became a finding: executionObligationOwnerToday reads 'Architecture + release engineering' while the five gate owner cells are heterogeneous and G05's is Component publisher + release. Read as a roll-up of gate owners that would be a real defect. It is not one — the string is byte-exact with DR-101's own owner cell, so the field is the row's execution owner. I record it because the finding would have been argued confidently and wrongly, and the check that killed it took one read.
